A coupling constant of about 16 Hz for the pair of vinylic protons is characteristic of a trans (E) double bond; cis (Z) alkenes usually give J ≈ 10 Hz.

The spectrum shows only four types of protons:

• 7.0 ppm (1 H, d, J = 16 Hz) – one vinylic H, trans-coupled  
• 5.5 ppm (1 H, dq) – the other vinylic H, coupled trans (J ≈ 16 Hz) to the 7 ppm H and coupled (J ≈ 7 Hz) to a methyl group  
• 2.1 ppm (3 H, s) – acetyl CH₃ of an acetate ester (–OCOCH₃)  
• 1.6 ppm (3 H, d) – CH₃ group on the alkene carbon (coupled to the 5.5 ppm vinylic H)

Only one alkene methyl and no extra CH₂ signals are present, so the olefinic side chain must be CH₃-CH=CH–O– rather than a four-carbon (butenyl) fragment.

Thus the compound is trans-propenyl acetate.

Answer: B
